content.text: The text is a compilation of historical, scientific, literary, religious, and fictional excerpts. It explains determining true meridians with Polaris, discusses pheasants, ginkgo trees, American woods, Irish history and legends, white mice, professions, and goose farming. Extensive passages from Robert Ingersoll criticize biblical authority, hell, slavery, religious intolerance, and dogma while praising reason, liberty, science, education, and humane morality. A later adventure follows Croyden and Macloud, who camp at Greenberry Point near Annapolis seeking Parmenter’s buried treasure, confront thieves, return to Hampton, and investigate attempted burglary and blackmail. Croyden receives an offer for worthless bonds, while Macloud pursues Elaine Carrington. Elaine Cavendish is invited from Northumberland to stay with Carrington at Ashburton, Hampton, hoping to reunite with Croyden.
